report.source_text: Her pathology showed that the left ovary displayed near-complete replacement by a diffuse proliferation of large somewhat pleomorphic cells (Figure 2), with prominent nucleoli (Figure 3), numerous mitotic figures, admixed body macrophages, and punctate areas of necrosis. Immunohistochemistry showed the malignant cells expressed PAX5, CD20, MYC (Figure 4), and BCL2 (weak 30%). Her Ki-67 proliferation index was greater than 90% (Figure 5). The cells were negative for AE1/AE3, S100, CD30, and cyclin D1.

clinician.final_diagnosis: High-grade CD20-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) of the left ovary, stage IV Lugano
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 48-year-old female presented with constitutional symptoms (generalized fatigue, 40 pounds unintentional weight loss) and lower abdominal discomfort. Imaging (CT abdomen and transvaginal ultrasound) revealed a left heterogeneous ovarian mass (4 × 4.2 cm on CT, 7.4 × 5.6 × 6.6 cm on ultrasound) and an enlarged left adrenal gland (1.5 × 2 cm). Pathology of the left ovarian mass confirmed high-grade DLBCL with diffuse proliferation of large pleomorphic cells, prominent nucleoli, numerous mitotic figures, and necrosis. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated CD20+, PAX5+, MYC+, and BCL2 weak (30%) expression with Ki-67 proliferation index >90%, confirming aggressive lymphoma. PET-CT staging identified extranodal involvement in the right maxillary sinus, establishing stage IV Lugano disease. The patient received dose-adjusted DA-EPOCH-R chemotherapy (6 cycles total), with PET-CT after 3 cycles showing interval resolution of hypermetabolic lesions in the right maxillary sinus. She achieved complete remission and remains in remission at 1.5 years post-treatment with serial PET monitoring.
